artboards.role: Forno Rosso pizzeria marketing home page: header, hero, delivery banner, featured-menu grid, brand story section, footer. The linked node is a single top-level FRAME (not a CANVAS with multiple pages), so the whole page is one artboard; header/hero/delivery-banner/featured-section/story-section/footer are internal regions of it, not separate artboards. MT-STORY-041 scopes implementation to the 'story-section' region (node 6:108) specifically; the rest of the page is mapped for completeness/context since it ships in the same frame.

excluded.reason: The Figma frame is a plain web page composition (1440px desktop artboard) with no simulated device chrome, browser frame, status bar, notch, or on-screen keyboard drawn into it — nothing to exclude on that basis.

open_questions.detail: The branch/ticket (MT-STORY-041-brand-story-section) names only the brand story section, but the ingested Figma node (6:6) is the entire home page and this map covers all 6 regions (header, hero, delivery-banner, featured-section, story-section, footer) per the mapping instructions, since they all live in one frame.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Treated the whole home-page frame as in-scope for MAPPING (so the implementer has full context and can see what BrandStorySection sits between), but flagged BrandStorySection (6:108) and its children as the PRIMARY build target implied by the ticket name.

open_questions.detail: The icon layer feeding the 'Authentic Neapolitan Woodfired' badge is named 'fire-extinguisher' in Figma, but the glyph and copy both point to a flame/fire icon (consistent with a wood-fired-oven brand), not a fire-extinguisher pictogram.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Mapped it to an icon named 'flame' in the Icon set rather than reproducing the literal Figma layer name, since shipping a fire-extinguisher glyph next to 'Authentic Neapolitan Woodfired' would visually contradict the copy.

open_questions.detail: The rendered PNG shows 'Estimated delivery: 30 mins' with '30 mins' in a green highlight colour, but node 6:21 in the Figma tree carries a single uniform white fill with no per-character style override (unlike the hero heading at 6:30, which does use characterStyleOverrides for its two-tone text).
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assumed the PNG is correct (it is authoritative for visuals) and specified the '30 mins' substring as a green-highlighted inline span in the Text component's props, rather than plain white text.

options.label: Split into two spans, '30 mins' in var(--brand-green) — matches figma-frame.png
Single uniform white run — matches the raw node 6:21 fill/lack of style overrides in figma-frame.json

open_questions.detail: Figma text nodes 6:77 ('Funghi Selvatici & Tartufo') and 6:101 ('Prosciutto Crudo e Rucola') store the full untruncated string, but the rendered PNG shows them ellipsis-truncated ('Funghi Selvatici &...', 'Prosciutto Crudo e...') because the title and price share a fixed-width row (262px) with justify-between.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implemented PizzaCard's title as single-line with CSS text-overflow: ellipsis so long names truncate against the price exactly as the PNG shows, rather than wrapping or shrinking the price.

open_questions.topic: Footer social icon: Twitter bird vs. X logo
open_questions.detail: Footer social node 6:149/6:604 is named 'twitter' and its vector paths draw the legacy bird glyph, not the current X wordmark/logo.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Shipped the bird glyph as drawn (figma-frame.png is authoritative for visuals) rather than substituting the modern X logo.

open_questions.detail: The 'F' brand mark (header 6:9/6:10, footer 6:140/6:141) is a plain text glyph in a coloured circle, not an imported SVG/logo asset — no logo file exists in figma-assets.json.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Built BrandLogo as a circular div with a text glyph (matches the Figma source exactly), not as an image, since no logo asset was exported.
